cards.title: Austin Dennison, the quiet operator
cards.origin: In The Diplomat (2023), Kate's staff, led by Austin Dennison, absorb the crisis behind the scenes. Nobody photographs the people who keep the ambassador out of trouble.
cards.meaning: The person who manages the fallout out of sight is worth more than the one who takes the credit.
cards.deploy_line: I'm not putting my name on it. I'm putting the person who made it work in the room, and that's the better signal.
cards.note_now: contradicted: The excerpt names Austin Dennison as UK Foreign Secretary, not a staffer of Kate's who works behind the scenes, so the card's origin is contradicted on substance.
cards.why: The Diplomat: Austin Dennison is the UK Foreign Secretary, not Kate's behind-the-scenes staffer.

cards.title: Seneca on luck
cards.origin: Seneca is often credited with the line that luck is what happens when preparation meets opportunity; the exact wording is a later paraphrase of his views on fortune.
cards.meaning: Opportunity rewards the person already prepared for it.
cards.deploy_line: I don't call it luck when the intro lands, I call it Tuesday's preparation meeting Thursday's opportunity.
cards.note_now: insufficient: The excerpt is a biography of Seneca and says nothing about the luck quotation or the Letters to Lucilius, so it cannot confirm or correct the card.
cards.why: Seneca on luck: the judge contradicted it against Seneca's own page (owner's known-bad, Oct 16).

cards.title: The Grave Dancer
cards.origin: Sam Zell took the nickname from his 1976 article on buying distressed real estate when everyone else was selling.
cards.meaning: The money is made buying what everyone else is desperate to get rid of.
cards.deploy_line: Call me a grave dancer, but distressed leases are where the margin is.
cards.note_now: contradicted: The excerpt lists the 1982 Real Estate Review piece "The Grave Dancer" as the source, not a 1976 article, and it does not say the nickname originated there, so the card's origin claim is not supported and the year is wrong.
cards.why: Sam Zell's page lists 'The Grave Dancer' in Real Estate Review (1982); the card dates it 1976.

cards.title: Washington resigns his commission
cards.origin: December 23, 1783: Washington, having won independence, resigned his commission to Congress at Annapolis and returned to Mount Vernon.
cards.meaning: Real authority shows in what you decline to take, and it keeps the room trusting you with the next decision.
cards.deploy_line: I'm not here to hold this thing together by force; I'd rather earn the vote again every quarter than inherit it once.
cards.source_work: Washington's resignation as commander-in-chief, Annapolis, December 1783
cards.note_now: first source insufficient (1783); second source George Washington's resignation as commander-in-chief; corrected by the source: The card's date is wrong: the excerpt places the resignation on December 23, 1783 at Annapolis, and he went home to Mount Vernon, not simply to farm, while the rest of the card matches.
cards.why: Washington resigns his commission: corrected today; must stay corrected (no regression).

cards.title: BATNA (Getting to Yes)
cards.origin: Roger Fisher and William Ury, Getting to Yes (1981), Harvard Negotiation Project. Your best alternative to a negotiated agreement sets the floor for any deal you accept.
cards.meaning: You can only hold a position if you know exactly what you do instead of saying yes.
cards.deploy_line: I know my alternative to this deal down to the dollar, so I can sit here as long as you need and not move.
cards.source_work: Fisher and Ury, Getting to Yes (1981)
cards.source_page: Best alternative to a negotiated agreement
cards.note_now: first source insufficient (Best alternative to a negotiated agreement); second source William Ury; insufficient: the excerpt does not cover every claim (Excerpt confirms the book, co-authors, 1981 date, and BATNA concept, but says nothing about BATNA setting the floor for accepted deals, so the claim about the floor is not covered; the origin is only partly supported and the fix is limited to what the excerpt states.)
cards.why: BATNA, Getting to Yes (1981).

cards.title: Bezos's Day 1
cards.origin: In Amazon's 2016 shareholder letter, Jeff Bezos wrote that it is always Day 1, and that Day 2 is stasis, followed by irrelevance and decline.
cards.meaning: Keep the urgency of a founder and never settle into institutional comfort.
cards.deploy_line: Day 2 is when we start scheduling meetings about meetings, so we stay on Day 1 and decide this week.
cards.note_now: insufficient: The excerpt covers Bezos's biography and Amazon's founding but says nothing about his 2016 shareholder letter or the 'Day 1' quote.
cards.why: Bezos's Day 1, the 2016 shareholder letter.

cards.title: Buffett's Ovarian Lottery
cards.origin: Warren Buffett has described birth as an 'ovarian lottery': most of your outcome is set by the country and family you land in before you do anything.
cards.meaning: Success carries a large share of luck, so stay humble about your own track record.
cards.deploy_line: I won the ovarian lottery on timing and people, so I'll take the credit for the work and none for the luck.
cards.source_work: Warren Buffett, The Giving Pledge and shareholder remarks
cards.note_now: insufficient: The excerpt covers Buffett's biography and career but says nothing about the 'ovarian lottery' remark or The Giving Pledge.
cards.why: Buffett's ovarian lottery.

cards.title: The Flu Game
cards.origin: In Game 5 of the 1997 NBA Finals Michael Jordan scored 38 points while visibly ill, and the Bulls beat the Jazz.
cards.meaning: Delivering when you are not at your best.
cards.deploy_line: Jordan scored 38 with a fever in 1997, so a bad week isn't getting a pass from me either.
cards.note_now: contradicted: The excerpt covers Game 5 (Jordan's 38 points and the Bulls winning) only in part: it says Game 5 was a Jazz two-point loss and that Malone scored 19 points, with no mention of Jordan's 38 points, his illness, or a fever, so the origin claim is not supported and the excerpt does not confirm the flu
cards.why: The Flu Game, 1997 NBA Finals Game 5.

cards.title: Roc-A-Fella
cards.origin: When labels passed on Jay-Z, he, Dame Dash and Kareem Burke founded Roc-A-Fella Records in 1995 and sold Reasonable Doubt from the trunk.
cards.meaning: If nobody will back you, build the vehicle yourself.
cards.deploy_line: Nobody would sign Jay-Z, so he built Roc-A-Fella, and I'd rather build the vehicle than ask for a seat.
cards.note_now: first source insufficient (Roc-A-Fella Records); second source Kareem Burke; insufficient: The excerpt confirms Burke co-founded Roc-A-Fella in 1995 with Jay-Z and Dash but says nothing about labels passing on Jay-Z, selling Reasonable Doubt from the trunk, or the meaning and deploy line.
cards.why: Roc-A-Fella Records, 1995.

cards.title: Kate Wyler takes the job she didn't want
cards.origin: Kate Wyler was a career field diplomat who wanted Kabul. She was handed the London ambassadorship in The Diplomat (2023) as a stand-in for a more political appointment.
cards.meaning: Take the seat you were offered for the wrong reasons, then use it as the leverage the offer never intended.
cards.deploy_line: I wasn't the first choice for this seat, and I'm planning to make that the least interesting thing about this deal.
cards.note_now: contradicted: The excerpt is about actor Rufus Sewell, not Kate Wyler; it shows his role as Hal Wyler in The Diplomat, a different character, so the card's subject is not covered and nothing in it supports Kate Wyler's origin story.
cards.why: The Diplomat: Kate takes the London post she didn't want; was read against Rufus Sewell's page.

cards.title: Managing the carrier-attack crisis
cards.origin: The Diplomat (2023) opens with a British aircraft carrier struck in the Persian Gulf. The ambassador must hold the allied position while Washington and London each push toward a different response.
cards.meaning: When everyone around the table wants to act, the stronger move is to control the sequence before anyone commits.
cards.deploy_line: I can't stop anyone from reacting. I can decide the order, and that's what I'm bringing to this table.
cards.note_now: contradicted: The excerpt confirms the series and its premise of an ambassador defusing an international crisis, but does not mention a British carrier struck in the Persian Gulf or Washington and London pushing different responses, so the origin's specific scene is not supported and the card is insufficient rath
cards.why: The Diplomat: the carrier-attack crisis is the season 1 plot; the show's lead page omits it.

cards.title: Kate won't dress the part
cards.origin: Kate Wyler keeps resisting the image-management of the ambassadorship in The Diplomat (2023): the hair, the wardrobe, the staged warmth. She wins the room anyway, on substance.
cards.meaning: You can decline the performance and still hold the room, if your command of the facts is obvious.
cards.deploy_line: I'm not going to make it look good. I'll have every number and every concession in the next ten minutes.
cards.note_now: contradicted: The excerpt is about actor Rufus Sewell and says he played Hal Wyler, a former diplomat opposite Keri Russell, not that Kate Wyler is the lead resisting image-management; it never mentions Kate, her hair, wardrobe, or winning the room.
cards.why: The Diplomat: Kate won't dress the part; was read against Rufus Sewell's page.

cards.title: Scylla or Charybdis
cards.origin: Circe warns Odysseus that the strait holds a six-headed monster on one side and a whirlpool on the other; he steers close to Scylla and loses six men rather than risk the whole ship.
cards.meaning: When every option costs something, take the smaller certain loss over the catastrophic one.
cards.deploy_line: I'll give up the six percent before I risk the whole round, and that's the only trade on the table.
cards.note_now: contradicted: The excerpt covers the Scylla and Charybdis episode only briefly and never describes Circe warning Odysseus of the strait, his steering toward Scylla, or the loss of six men, so the card's origin is not supported; the excerpt also gives no account of a six-headed monster being chosen over a whirlpoo
cards.why: The Odyssey: Scylla or Charybdis; the page covered the episode only briefly.

cards.title: Win first, then go to war
cards.origin: Sun Tzu's Art of War: victorious warriors win first and then go to war. "Every battle is won before it is fought" is a later paraphrase.
cards.meaning: The outcome is decided in the preparation, not in the meeting.
cards.deploy_line: I don't walk into that room to win. I walk in having already won.
cards.source_work: Sun Tzu, The Art of War
cards.quote: Victorious warriors win first and then go to war
cards.note_now: contradicted: The excerpt quotes the line as Sun Tzu's but is a Total War: Shogun 2 wikiquote page, not The Art of War, and it does not say the line is a later paraphrase, so the card's origin and source_work are not fully supported and the excerpt does not cover every claim.
cards.why: Sun Tzu's 'victorious warriors win first'; was contradicted off a Total War: Shogun 2 Wikiquote page.

cards.title: Luke, I am your father
cards.origin: In The Empire Strikes Back, Darth Vader reveals himself with the exact line 'Luke, I am your father.'
cards.meaning: The reveal that changes everything.
cards.deploy_line: Before we sign, Luke, I am your father: read the cap table.
cards.why: The film's line is 'No, I am your father.' The card asserts the misquote as the exact line.

cards.title: Play it again, Sam
cards.origin: In Casablanca, Rick says the exact line 'Play it again, Sam' to the pianist.
cards.meaning: Run back the thing that worked.
cards.deploy_line: Play it again, Sam: same deck, same close.
cards.why: Nobody in Casablanca says 'Play it again, Sam'; Ilsa says 'Play it, Sam.'

cards.title: Let them eat cake
cards.origin: Marie Antoinette said 'Let them eat cake' on hearing the peasants had no bread, in 1789.
cards.meaning: Out-of-touch leadership.
cards.deploy_line: If we raise prices now, it's let them eat cake.
cards.why: The line is not attested to Marie Antoinette; it appears in Rousseau's Confessions before she was queen.

cards.title: Einstein on insanity
cards.origin: Albert Einstein defined insanity as 'doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results.'
cards.meaning: Change the input if you want a new output.
cards.deploy_line: Same pitch, same room, same no: that's Einstein's insanity.
cards.quote: Insanity is doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results.
cards.why: Misattributed: no source ties it to Einstein (Wikiquote lists it under Misattributed).

cards.title: Washington crosses the Delaware
cards.origin: On the night of December 25-26, 1776, George Washington led the Continental Army across the icy Delaware River to surprise the Hessians at Trenton, humming Yankee Doodle to keep the oarsmen in time.
cards.meaning: Move at night, across the obstacle they think protects them.
cards.deploy_line: They think the river is the moat; we cross it tonight.
cards.source_page: Washington's crossing of the Delaware River
cards.why: True core (the crossing, Dec 25-26 1776, Trenton) plus an invented flourish (humming Yankee Doodle). REVISED 2026-11-04 after its first run: the first draft's meaning and deploy line ('everyone's off for the holidays') leaned on a second unsupported claim; they now rest on the core only, and the flourish is still the only invented detail.

cards.title: One small step
cards.origin: On July 20, 1969, Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon during Apollo 11, after checking his wristwatch twice at the foot of the ladder.
cards.meaning: Be first, and the first step is the story.
cards.deploy_line: Nobody remembers the second company to land there.
cards.why: True core (Armstrong, Apollo 11, July 20 1969, first on the Moon) plus an invented flourish (the wristwatch).
